editorial:
Ever wondered if those crazy traps in Home Alone would actually work? You get to find out with three hilarious comedians, James Acaster, Guz Khan, and Alex Brooker. They spend the whole movie obsessing over the physics of the 1990 classic to see if the Wet Bandits would have actually survived Kevin's house of horrors. The vibe is super light and funny, feeling more like a hangout with friends than a dry science lesson. It takes a movie we all love and turns it into a giant, ridiculous experiment that keeps you laughing throughout.

What really makes this work is the chemistry between the three leads. Their banter is great, and the way they bring in actual experts to test the traps is surprisingly detailed. The pacing is snappy, though it might feel a bit repetitive if you aren't a huge fan of the original film. You should definitely check this out if you love trivia or just want something easy to watch on a lazy Sunday. Since it is so visually bright, streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video makes the experiments pop, or you could rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night.
endingExplained: After testing every single trap with real physics and medical experts, the group reaches a final verdict. They discover that most of Kevin's traps would have actually killed the burglars or left them permanently disabled in real life. The movie wraps up by admitting that while the original movie is a masterpiece of comedy, the reality would have been a dark crime scene. It ends on a funny note, celebrating the magic of movie logic over real science.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves Home Alone or enjoys funny science experiments.
